sections.name: Bowser Space
sections.card:
Summary: At night in Party Mode the Donkey Kong Spaces of the day turn into Bowser Spaces, and landing on one makes Bowser hold a mini-game or a Bowser Bonus that can cost you coins, Orbs or a Star.
Weak points: Win the Bowser mini-game: only the players who lose pay him, in coins or Orbs, and the winners keep theirs. Landing with no coins is harmless: he hands you 10 coins and runs neither a mini-game nor a Bonus.
Tips: In the Bowser Bonus he strikes a special Dice Block that can land on 5, 10, 20 or 30 coins, or a Star, and whoever stopped there loses that amount. A Star result costs nothing if you hold no Star. Clockwork Castle has no Bowser Spaces.

sections.name: DK Space
sections.card:
Summary: By day, the Donkey Kong Spaces on a Party Mode board bring Donkey Kong in for an event: a mini-game where players trade bananas for coins, or a DK Bonus for the player who landed.
Looks like: A yellow-orange space showing Donkey Kong's face. No other game colours these spaces yellow-orange; elsewhere they are blue.
Tips: The DK Bonus here rolls a barrel-shaped Dice Block worth 5, 10, 20 or 30 coins, or a Star. Night swaps every DK Space for a Bowser Space. Clockwork Castle has none, because Donkey Kong and Bowser both turn up on that board.

sections.name: Chain Chomp
sections.card:
Summary: On Snowflake Lake, Chain Chomps live in the board's four doghouses, and a player who pays to ride one steals a Star from every rival it passes. Stars cannot be bought on this board.
Weak points: A Snack Orb stops a Chain Chomp's theft: you toss a bone, the Chomp leaps over your space to fetch it and keeps moving, and anyone sharing your space is spared as well. Team games have one catch: teammates share Orbs and cannot trap each other, yet a teammate's Chain Chomp ride can still burn through your Snack Orb.
Looks like: A metal ball, black or deep blue, with wide round eyes and a huge mouth of razor-sharp teeth; many are bigger than Mario.
Tips: Everyone starts with 5 Stars, more when a Star handicap is set. A Chain Chomp rider flattens whoever it reaches, teammates included, and takes their Star. Riding costs coins, and the price at night differs from the daytime one.

sections.name: Pink Boo
sections.card:
Summary: A pink Boo who steals for hire at night, found only on Towering Treetop and Castaway Bay. Pay 5 coins to have her take coins from a player, or 40 to have her take a Star.
Weak points: Holding a Boo-Away Orb blocks her theft from you; it triggers automatically, so you cannot throw it onto a space or use it yourself. She works only at night.
Looks like: A pink Boo, sometimes a light red one.
Tips: She does the ordinary Boo's old job here, since Boo has become a playable character. You can buy the Boo-Away Orb only on her two boards, at 10 coins.

sections.name: Evil Woody
sections.card:
Summary: At night the tree at the top of Towering Treetop is Evil Woody instead of Woody, and the ? Space beside him rains Spiny eggs that make every player lose coins, where Woody's daytime shower gives coins.
Looks like: A tree whose face always looks angry, coloured blue with purple leaves, which is Woody's palette turned around.
Tips: Day gives way to night every three turns. A meter at the start of each turn counts the turns left, which helps you pick when to step on that space. At night the Spiny shower hits every player, not only the one who landed, while by day the same space gives coins to all.

sections.name: Whomp
sections.card:
Summary: Mario Party 6 has two Whomps that block a path: one on Snowflake Lake, one on Faire Square. Each charges 10 coins to let you pass.
Looks like: A big stone slab shaped like a rectangle, with a permanent scowl, glowing red eyes, five crooked teeth in an open mouth, plain arms and feet without legs.
Tips: On Snowflake Lake the Whomp stands just before an Orb Shop, and getting past him leaves you on the right of the frozen pond. On Faire Square he blocks a path through the board's centre; paying lets you hop back to Brighton or Twila fast for another shot at Stars, which can save turns.

sections.name: Freezie
sections.card:
Summary: Snowflake Lake's nights bring big Freezies that close off the routes toward the board's centre; they thaw once daylight returns.
Weak points: Daylight melts them, so head for the centre during the day, when nothing blocks the routes.
Looks like: A big figure formed wholly from ice, wearing a puzzled look.
Tips: The time of day flips every three turns, and the pause menu tells you how many remain until the next flip. Stepping on a ? Space beside the frozen pond starts a coin game; at night it is a snowball fight in which players knock coins loose from one another.

sections.name: Shadow Star Space
sections.card:
Summary: The reverse of a Star Space: stopping here saddles you with a Shadow Star, taking a Star from you, or coins when you hold none. In this game only two boards use it: Castaway Bay and Clockwork Castle.
Weak points: On Castaway Bay the Shadow Star comes from Bowser on his Battle Yacht. Landing on a ? Space on a pole marked with a Star Space symbol swaps the two boats.
Tips: On Castaway Bay a player with no Star pays 20 coins instead. On Clockwork Castle DK turns into Bowser at night, and he is the one who hands out the Shadow Star.

sections.name: Bullet Bill Orb
sections.card:
Summary: A green Orb that only works on yourself and steals coins from the opponents you pass.
Uses: Any opponent you pass loses 20 coins to you. It also carries you over roadblocks without setting them off. On Faire Square, where rivals bunch up in the middle of the board, it can hit them for a lot of coins.
Tips: Only E. Gadd's Garage and Faire Square sell it. An Orb hut charges 20 coins, or 10 in a flash sale. Use it close to the Star Space and you sail past the Star, so hold it back when you mean to buy one.

sections.name: Flutter Orb
sections.card:
Summary: A green Orb that takes you straight to the Star Space.
Uses: Only you can be its target. Towering Treetop and E. Gadd's Garage, the boards that sell it, put the Star somewhere new once it has been bought.
Tips: An Orb hut sells it for 30 coins. A Star costs 20 coins on Towering Treetop, and E. Gadd's Garage works the same way.

sections.name: Metal Mushroom Orb
sections.card:
Summary: A green Orb that turns the player who uses it into metal.
Uses: Under a Metal Mushroom Orb, a Thwomp bounces off, a Tweester fizzles out, a Podoboo's fire does nothing, you kick a Bob-omb aside, a Koopa Troopa cannot carry something so heavy and quits, and a Zap Orb's Amps vanish after a failed zap.
Tips: Every board has it except Towering Treetop and Faire Square, and the board pages say that makes roadblocks there especially tough to dodge.

sections.name: Thwomp Orb
sections.card:
Summary: A red Orb that goes on a space and acts as a roadblock. An opponent passing over gets squashed by a Thwomp and their move ends there.
Uses: Leave it on a space your rivals have to cross. On Faire Square it can keep a player from buying Stars, most of all at night when Stars may be cheaper, and players often place it on the Red Space just ahead of the fixed Star space.
Tips: An Orb hut sells it for 10 coins, 5 during a flash sale, and the boards that stock it are Towering Treetop, Faire Square and Clockwork Castle. A rival under a Metal Mushroom Orb walks through unharmed, and you cannot put a new roadblock on top of one until an opponent has set it off.

sections.name: Piranha Plant Orb
sections.card:
Summary: A yellow Orb that can only be placed on a space. A Piranha Plant bites a rival who stops there, and that rival hands you half their coins.
Uses: Put it where rivals tend to stop. Landing on your own Orb gives you 5 coins. If you are already on the space when a rival lands, the plant goes for the rival alone.
Tips: It costs 15 coins, and every board sells it apart from Towering Treetop and Castaway Bay. It reacts to anyone who stops on the space, and remains until another Orb replaces it or a Star Space turns up on that square.

sections.name: Snack Orb
sections.card:
Summary: A blue Orb found only on Snowflake Lake that protects you from Chain Chomp.
Uses: Just carry one around; you cannot throw it onto a space or use it yourself. When a rival's Chain Chomp comes for you, it triggers by itself: you toss a bone, the Chomp hops over your space to fetch it, and anybody else standing there is spared as well. You can discard the Orb at any time. On a team, even a teammate's Chain Chomp ride can burn your Snack Orb.
Tips: An Orb hut charges 10 coins.

sections.name: Boo-Away Orb
sections.card:
Summary: A blue Orb that protects you from Pink Boo. It works on its own, so there is nothing for you to use or throw.
Uses: Keep one in hand on Towering Treetop or Castaway Bay and it fires on its own when a rival pays Pink Boo to come after you. It is the Gaddlight from earlier games, a flashlight whose beam frightens Boo off. You may discard the Orb whenever you want.
Tips: An Orb hut charges 10 coins. Only the two boards that have Pink Boo, Towering Treetop and Castaway Bay, stock it.
